note: The E shape of CAGED: open E moved up as a barre (its chord boxes pinned, so they stay the lesson's shapes), then the chord, arpeggio, major pentatonic and major scale in the same frets, the arpeggio alone, and the shape strummed then picked on two chords. The old Key selector is now moves (any key), so the text names the key only as {{=key}}, the chords in time are chord tokens, and a {{?key}} line says what stays the same.

exercise.title: CAGED: the E shape
exercise.why: A barre chord with its root on the low E string is the open E chord moved up the neck, so everything that sits around open E, its arpeggio, its pentatonic and its scale, moves up with it.

cells.text:
Press the chord box below to hear E. Then press the three chord boxes under it: each is the same shape moved up the neck, with finger 1 in place of the nut.
Play all four, and say each chord's name as you land on it: the name is the note under finger 1 on the low E string.

Press Play on each of the four panels below to hear it: the {{=key}} chord in the E shape, its arpeggio, the {{=key}} major pentatonic scale and the {{=key}} major scale, all in the same frets.
Play each one on your guitar, starting and ending on a root.
Practice until you can see the chord inside the scale.
{{?key}}In another key the shape moves along the neck, and every note keeps its place inside it.

Press Play below to hear the {{=key}} arpeggio run up and back down. Then play it yourself, from the lowest ringed {{1}} to the highest note and back.
Practice until your fingers find the next note without you looking.

The tab below holds two chords in the E shape: {{chord:I}}, the 1st chord of the key, built on {{1}}, and {{chord:II}}, the same shape two frets up.
Press Play below to start the backing track. On each chord, strum the shape on beat 1, then pick three of its notes, one per beat.
When you change the chord, the whole shape moves and the notes keep their places inside it.
